speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack, I am concerned about blood flow to your intestines. Do you have any history of atrial fibrillation or other heart rhythm irregularities?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain seem disproportionately severe compared to what you can feel on physical exam, and do you have a known history of atrial fibrillation or other cardiac arrhythmias?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. History of acute myocardial infarction. Social history: Smokes 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent MI, smoking history, and symptoms of severe pain with bloody stools, I suspect acute mesenteric ischemia. REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the abdomen and pelvis.
